scenes.dialogue: Every civil case in India begins with one question. Not 'Who is right?' Not 'How much can I claim?'
scenes.spoken: Every civil case in India begins with one question. Not 'Who is right?' Not 'How much can I claim?'

scenes.dialogue: The first question is: do you have a cause of action? Get this wrong, and your suit can be thrown out before the defendant even files a written statement.
scenes.spoken: The first question is: do you have a cause of action? Get this wrong, and your suit can be thrown out before the defendant even files a written statement.

scenes.dialogue: So in the next five minutes: what a cause of action is, how to spot one, and why it matters at every stage of a suit.
scenes.spoken: So in the next five minutes: what a cause of action is, how to spot one, and why it matters at every stage of a suit.

scenes.dialogue: Surprisingly, the Code of Civil Procedure never defines the term. The definition comes from the courts.
scenes.spoken: Surprisingly, the Code of Civil Procedure never defines the term. The definition comes from the courts.

scenes.dialogue: The classic statement comes from an English case, Read versus Brown, decided in 1888.
scenes.spoken: The classic statement comes from an English case, Read versus Brown, decided in eighteen eighty-eight.

scenes.dialogue: A cause of action is every fact the plaintiff would have to prove, if it were denied, to win judgment.
scenes.spoken: A cause of action is every fact the plaintiff would have to prove, if it were denied, to win judgment.

scenes.dialogue: Our Supreme Court adopted this in A B C Laminart versus A P Agencies.
scenes.spoken: Our Supreme Court adopted this in A B C Laminart versus A P Agencies.

scenes.dialogue: And put it simply: a bundle of facts which, with the law that applies to them, gives the plaintiff a right to relief against the defendant.
scenes.spoken: And put it simply: a bundle of facts which, with the law that applies to them, gives the plaintiff a right to relief against the defendant.

scenes.dialogue: Notice the words 'bundle of facts'. Not one fact. Every fact you need, taken together.
scenes.spoken: Notice the words 'bundle of facts'. Not one fact. Every fact you need, taken together.

scenes.dialogue: Open the bundle, and you will usually find two things. First, a right that belongs to the plaintiff.
scenes.spoken: Open the bundle, and you will usually find two things. First, a right that belongs to the plaintiff.

scenes.dialogue: Second, an act or omission of the defendant that infringes that right.
scenes.spoken: Second, an act or omission of the defendant that infringes that right.

scenes.dialogue: A right with no breach gives you nothing to sue on. A breach that touches no right of yours gives you nothing either.
scenes.spoken: A right with no breach gives you nothing to sue on. A breach that touches no right of yours gives you nothing either.

scenes.dialogue: You need both, and against this defendant. Let's make it concrete. Ravi lends five lakh rupees to Suresh.
scenes.spoken: You need both, and against this defendant. Let's make it concrete. Ravi lends five lakh rupees to Suresh.

scenes.dialogue: Suresh promises to repay by 31st March 2025. The date passes. Suresh pays nothing.
scenes.spoken: Suresh promises to repay by thirty-first March, twenty twenty-five. The date passes. Suresh pays nothing.

scenes.dialogue: What must Ravi prove? One, he gave the loan. Two, Suresh agreed to repay by that date.
scenes.spoken: What must Ravi prove? One, he gave the loan. Two, Suresh agreed to repay by that date.

scenes.dialogue: Three, the date has passed. Four, the money is still unpaid.
scenes.spoken: Three, the date has passed. Four, the money is still unpaid.

scenes.dialogue: Each of these is part of the bundle. Together, they are Ravi's cause of action.
scenes.spoken: Each of these is part of the bundle. Together, they are Ravi's cause of action.

scenes.dialogue: It arose on 31st March 2025, the due date he missed. Remember that date. We'll need it.
scenes.spoken: It arose on thirty-first March, twenty twenty-five, the due date he missed. Remember that date. We'll need it.

scenes.dialogue: Two common mistakes. First, the cause of action does not depend on the defence.
scenes.spoken: Two common mistakes. First, the cause of action does not depend on the defence.

scenes.dialogue: The Privy Council said in Chand Kour versus Partab Singh that it refers entirely to the grounds set out in the plaint.
scenes.spoken: The Privy Council said in Chand Kour versus Partab Singh that it refers entirely to the grounds set out in the plaint.

scenes.dialogue: Second, it is not the relief. The relief is what you want from the court.
scenes.spoken: Second, it is not the relief. The relief is what you want from the court.

scenes.dialogue: The cause of action is why you are entitled to it. So why does this matter so much? Five reasons.
scenes.spoken: The cause of action is why you are entitled to it. So why does this matter so much? Five reasons.

scenes.dialogue: One: pleading. Order 7 Rule 1(e) requires every plaint to state the facts constituting the cause of action, and when it arose.
scenes.spoken: One: pleading. Order Seven, Rule One E, requires every plaint to state the facts constituting the cause of action, and when it arose.

scenes.dialogue: Two: rejection. Under Order 7 Rule 11(a), a plaint that discloses no cause of action must be rejected.
scenes.spoken: Two: rejection. Under Order Seven, Rule Eleven A, a plaint that discloses no cause of action must be rejected.

scenes.dialogue: The court reads only the plaint and its documents, not the defence.
scenes.spoken: The court reads only the plaint and its documents, not the defence.

scenes.dialogue: And as Justice Krishna Iyer put it, if clever drafting creates only an illusion of a cause of action, nip it in the bud.
scenes.spoken: And as Justice Krishna Iyer put it, if clever drafting creates only an illusion of a cause of action, nip it in the bud.

scenes.dialogue: Three: jurisdiction. Besides where the defendant lives, Section 20(c) lets you sue where the cause of action arises, wholly or in part.
scenes.spoken: Three: jurisdiction. Besides where the defendant lives, Section Twenty C lets you sue where the cause of action arises, wholly or in part.

scenes.dialogue: In Ravi's case, that can include where the loan was given, or where repayment was due. Four: one suit for the whole claim.
scenes.spoken: In Ravi's case, that can include where the loan was given, or where repayment was due. Four: one suit for the whole claim.

scenes.dialogue: Under Order 2 Rule 2, if Ravi sues for only three lakh, he cannot later sue for the other two.
scenes.spoken: Under Order Two, Rule Two, if Ravi sues for only three lakh, he cannot later sue for the other two.

scenes.dialogue: And a relief he leaves out without the court's leave is lost for good.
scenes.spoken: And a relief he leaves out without the court's leave is lost for good.

scenes.dialogue: Five: limitation. For many suits, the limitation clock starts when the cause of action arises.
scenes.spoken: Five: limitation. For many suits, the limitation clock starts when the cause of action arises.

scenes.dialogue: The Limitation Act fixes the exact starting point for each kind of suit. That's why we pinned 31st March 2025.
scenes.spoken: The Limitation Act fixes the exact starting point for each kind of suit. That's why we pinned thirty-first March, twenty twenty-five.

scenes.dialogue: So before you draft any plaint, ask three questions. What right does my client have?
scenes.spoken: So before you draft any plaint, ask three questions. What right does my client have?

scenes.dialogue: What did the defendant do, or fail to do, that breached it? And when and where did that happen?
scenes.spoken: What did the defendant do, or fail to do, that breached it? And when and where did that happen?

scenes.dialogue: If you can answer all three with facts you can prove, you have a cause of action.
scenes.spoken: If you can answer all three with facts you can prove, you have a cause of action.

scenes.dialogue: If you can't, no amount of drafting will save the suit. See you in the next episode.
scenes.spoken: If you can't, no amount of drafting will save the suit. See you in the next episode.
